newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Americans chose Valentine tulips from Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Americans chose Valentine tulips from Amsterdam.

text.p: Romantic Americans eager to have tulips from Amsterdam are ensuring a busy week for Zurel, a leading Dutch flower exporter, said the company's airfreight manager, Roel van Rossum.
Currently, the Aalsmeer-headquartered company is handling 35 tonnes of flowers daily in the run up to St Valentine's day.
Van Rossum said there was more demand for Valentine's day flowers this year, adding tulips and roses were the favourites.
He estimated that business is up 10 to 20 percent on last year, with more demand especially coming from Asian countries such as Singapore, Hong Kong and Thailand.
"A couple of years ago there was virtually nothing from countries such as Thailand and Taipei but Valentine's Day is becoming bigger in those countries now," he added.
There is also a trend for more flowers to be imported from countries such as Colombia, Ecuador, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Kenya, he said.
Approximately eight to 10 percent of Zurel's business is shipped by air. The company is one of the world's largest flower exporters and employs around 600 people.

Demand for airfreight is also increasing, even within Europe. For instance, flowers are being sent by air to Athens, Helsinki, Moscow and the Czech Republic, he said. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+ 5017
